headline: School lunch in Japan, an old cinema and the wrong bag
teaser: Who cleans the classroom in Japan? What was the cinema like 60 years ago? Why is there a box of dog biscuits in Mia's bag?

articles.title: A School Day in Japan
articles.dek: Indoor shoes, lunch in the classroom and cleaning time: meet Haruto.

sources.name: The Japan Forum: Changing our shoes

paras: What is a school day like for a teenager in Japan? Meet Haruto. He is thirteen, and he lives in Osaka. His school day has got a lot of things that may surprise you.

Haruto walks to school with some friends. When he arrives, he doesn't go straight into his classroom. First, he takes off his outdoor shoes and puts them in a small locker. Then he puts on a pair of indoor shoes. In this way, the students don't bring much dirt into the school.
Lessons start at about half past eight. Haruto has six lessons a day. His favourite subject is science. He doesn't like maths very much, but he always does his homework.

At lunchtime, the students don't go to a dining room. They eat in their classroom. Some students put on white coats and caps. They bring the food from the kitchen and serve it to their classmates. Today there is some rice, a bowl of soup, some fish and a carton of milk. 'There isn't much meat today,' Haruto says, 'but there are a lot of vegetables.' Everybody eats the same food.

After lunch, there isn't any time to play. It is cleaning time! In many Japanese schools, the students clean their classrooms themselves. Haruto takes a broom and sweeps the floor. His friend Yui cleans the board. Two other students wipe the floor in the hall. It takes about fifteen minutes.

Why do they do it? Teachers say that cleaning teaches students to work together. Students also learn to look after their school. 'At first I didn't like it,' says Haruto. 'Now I don't mind. Our classroom is always clean!'
Here is one more fact. The school year in Japan doesn't start in September. It starts in April. How many differences can you find between Haruto's school and yours?

articles.title: When the Cinema Was Magic
articles.dek: Mr Haddad is 72. He tells us about the old cinema in his town.
paras: Mr Omar Haddad is seventy-two. When he was a boy, not many families had a TV at home. But there was a big cinema in his town. Our school reporter, Lily, asked him about it.
Lily: Where was the cinema, Mr Haddad? Omar: It was in the main square, next to the bank. It was a beautiful old building with red doors. There were about four hundred seats inside.
Lily: How often did you go there? Omar: Every Saturday afternoon. Tickets were very cheap. My friends and I were always in the front row. We were very noisy, too!

Lily: Were the films in colour? Omar: Some films were in colour, but a lot of them were black and white. Before the film, there was always a short news programme. It was the only way to see the news with pictures.

Lily: What was your favourite film? Omar: That's easy. It was a cowboy film. I was nine, and I was so excited. The horses on the big screen were enormous! After the film, we were cowboys in the street all evening.

Lily: Is the cinema still there? Omar: No, it isn't. It closed a long time ago, and now the building is a supermarket. I was sad when it closed. But last month I was at the new cinema in the shopping centre with my granddaughter. The seats were very comfortable, and the sound was great. It wasn't the same, but it was a lovely afternoon.
Lily: Which is better, the cinema or TV at home? Omar: For me, the cinema. A big screen and a dark room are magic. You forget everything else for two hours.

grammar.point: Past simple of be: was / were

articles.title: The Wrong Bag
articles.dek: Mia bought a present for Mum. But what is inside her shopping bag?
paras: Last Saturday, Mia went to the shopping centre with her brother, Leo. It was their mum's birthday on Sunday, and they wanted to buy her a present. They looked in a lot of shops. Finally, they found a soft blue jumper. It cost twenty-five pounds. Mia paid for it, and the shop assistant put it in a big green bag.

After that, they were hungry, so they went to a café. Mia put the green bag under the table. They ordered two hot chocolates and talked about the party. The café was very busy. An old man sat at the next table. He had a green bag too, but Mia didn't notice it.
When they got home, Mia opened the bag. She wanted to wrap the present. But there was no jumper inside! There was a big box of dog biscuits and a red ball. 'Oh no!' she shouted. 'This isn't our bag!'
Leo thought for a moment. 'The man in the café!' he said. 'He took our bag, and we took his.' Mia felt terrible. The party was the next day. What could they do?

Then Mia saw a piece of paper in the bag. It was a receipt from a pet shop, and it had a phone number on it. She called the number. A woman answered. 'Yes, my dad was in that café,' she said. 'He came home with a jumper. He was very surprised!'

The next morning, Mia and Leo met the old man and his daughter outside the café. His name was Mr Kim. He gave them the jumper, and they gave him the dog biscuits. 'My dog Buster was very sad last night,' he laughed. 'He doesn't wear jumpers, but he loves biscuits!'
In the afternoon, Mum opened her present and smiled. 'It's beautiful!' she said. Mia and Leo looked at each other and laughed. Now they never put their shopping bags on the floor.

grammar.point: Past simple: regular and irregular verbs
grammar.rule: Regular verbs add -ed in the past: look → looked, open → opened. Many common verbs are irregular, so learn them: go → went, buy → bought, take → took. The past form is the same for I, you, he, she, we and they.

kps.fact: At home, Mia found dog biscuits in the bag, not the jumper.
kps.q: What was in the wrong bag?

kps.fact: A receipt in the bag had a phone number on it.
kps.q: How did Mia find Mr Kim?
opts: She went back to the shop.
She called the number on a receipt.

kps.fact: They changed bags the next morning, and Mum loved her present.
kps.q: What did Mum say about the jumper?

mindmap.question: How did Mia get Mum's present back?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the story.
summary.model: Mia took the wrong bag in a café, so she lost Mum's present. She found a phone number on a receipt, and she got the jumper back.

options.t: Mia and Leo bought a jumper for their mum's birthday.
options.why: This is how the story starts.
options.evidence: Finally, they found a soft blue jumper.

options.t: They took an old man's bag by mistake in a café.
options.why: This is the problem in the story.
options.evidence: 'He took our bag, and we took his.'

options.t: A receipt helped them find the man and get the jumper back.
options.why: This is how the problem ends.
options.evidence: He gave them the jumper, and they gave him the dog biscuits.

options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.

options.t: Mum wanted a new dog for her birthday.
Mia saw the old man's bag and took it on purpose.
options.why: Wrong: Mia didn't notice the other bag.
options.evidence: He had a green bag too, but Mia didn't notice it.

speak.p: Did you ever lose something when you went shopping? What happened?
speak.hint: Once I lost my… / In the end, I found it…

write.p: Write a short story that begins: 'When I got home, I opened my shopping bag.' Write 35 words or more.
steps: Say what you bought and where.
Say what was wrong with the bag.
